title: Why he left Agabama in 1936
summary: Dissatisfied as danzonete and charangas took over, he quit the sextet to work for his father; the Lopez-Barroso charanga is described.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Okay. All right. In 1936, you left Agabama. Why?
Because - ah - I wasn't satisfied with what's going on and I went to work with my father to satisfy my father because he want me to ......
Sentimental-wise because I was the main thing in my father's business, because he was very liberal....
No, but you, you mentioned before you went there, you were dissatisfied. Can you tell me why?

Ah - well, because in those days they start the danzonete and the charanga with singers and he was taking care, a charanga that they create with, with Cachao's brother, he was a pianist and they made a tremendous.......
Oh yeah, that's right, Barroso and ah---

Cachao's brother, Cachao was the bass player, and Macho, his brother was the pianist and Manolito was the flute player and Miguelito Valdes was the violin player and the timbales was Barberito and the guiro was Carl the one that then played with Arcano.
Okay, so that's probably why Agadama broke up then, right?
